series.$note: series.observed holds several sources and must not be read as one curve. DS-35: All greenhouse gases including land-use change, GWP100 (OWID, from Climate Watch / PIK), from 1990. DS-02: Asset-level observed emissions, CO₂e GWP100 (Climate TRACE); land use accounted differently from OWID, 2015-2025. DS-40: Total GHG emissions including LULUCF/LUCF exactly as the Party submitted them to the UNFCCC, on that Party’s own reporting guidelines and GWP set (UNFCCC Data Interface, snapshot of 2024-07-05). Non-Annex I Parties report only the years their national communications cover, and the figure is negative where reported removals exceed reported emissions. Points from an NDC document are that document's own inventory basis. The same year can appear more than once with different values; R3 keeps them side by side and never averages them.

ndc_assessment.vintage: First (I)NDC round, as assessed by WRI CAIT (2016). Not the latest submission.
ndc_assessment.summary: "Jamaica's intended nationally determined contribution covers actions in the energy sector (IPCC source category 1)" which will unconditionally "mitigate the equivalent of 1.1 million metric tons of carbon dioxide per year by 2030 versus the BAU scenario. This is a reduction of 7.8% of emissions versus BAU." "Jamaica will conditionally increase its ambition to a reduction of GHG emissions of 10% below the BAU scenario, subject to the provision of international support." The INDC also includes a section on adaptation.
ndc_assessment.ghg_target: Mitigate 1.1 MtCO2e (unconditional) per year by 2030 compared to the BAU scenario, or 7.8% (unconditional) to 10% (conditional) reduction in GHG emissions by 2030 compared to the BAU scenario
ndc_assessment.gases: CO2, CH4, N2O, SO2, NOx, CO, NMVOCs
ndc_assessment.$note: Third-party assessment of the first (I)NDC round. It is not merged into ndc.*, is not used by derive(), and does not appear on the dial as a target.

evidence.sentence: By 2030, it foresees emission reductions covering these two sectors of between 25.4 per cent (unconditional) and 28.5 per cent (conditional) relative to a business-as-usual scenario (which takes into account policies in place as of 2005).

• 25.4% reduction relative to business-as-usual emissions in 2030 without international support (unconditional) • 28.5% reduction relative to business-as-usual emissions in 2030 conditional upon international support The source data is that reported in Jamaica's Third National Communication and 2018

emissions_profile.$note: Headline totals are OWID only. OWID's CO₂ sub-totals are fossil/industrial CO₂ by fuel, not a full sectoral GHG breakdown, and do not sum to total_mtco2e. DS-05's rows are non-CO₂ gases only and are not comparable with the others; that is also why DS-05 is absent from series.observed, where a shorter curve would read as a disagreement rather than a difference of scope. by_source carries each source whole.

verdict.text: The registry's current submission for this Party is NDC 3.0, filed 2025-09-22. 53 observed values are loaded from DS-02 (11), DS-35 (35), DS-40 (7). For 2024 the sources disagree: DS-02 13.2 MtCO₂e, DS-35 9.1 MtCO₂e. They are on different inventory scopes and the engine does not reconcile them. No implementation gap is reported: 35 observed years are loaded, but no NDC target emissions figure has been parsed, so there is nothing to measure the trend against. ND-GAIN scores it 47.5 for 2024. In the first NDC round, WRI's CAIT assessment recorded: Mitigate 1.1 MtCO2e (unconditional) per year by 2030 compared to the BAU scenario, or 7.8% (unconditional) to 10% (conditional) reduction in GHG emissions by 2030 compared to the BAU scenario It was classed both. That is a 2016 assessment of an earlier submission, not the target above. Projected warming for 2080-2099 against 1995-2014 ranges from +1.02°C under SSP1-2.6 to +3.33°C under SSP5-8.5. These are model runs, not observations.
